draft.title: Effects of the conflict
card: The conflict in Indochina killed millions of people, both soldiers and civilians, across Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia. Estimates vary, so historians give a range rather than one number.
The land was damaged by heavy bombing and by chemicals. The US sprayed herbicides such as Agent Orange to strip leaves from forests that gave cover to enemy troops.
Unexploded bombs and damaged farmland stayed dangerous and hard to use for years after the fighting ended.
After 1975, many people left Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia, and many fled Vietnam by boat. Some were resettled in other countries, including Australia, where they changed the make-up of the population.
draft.remember: The conflict left deaths, damaged land and refugees, and its effects reached Australia.

a.q: Why did the US spray herbicides such as Agent Orange in Vietnam?
opts: To remove forest cover that hid enemy troops
To destroy the cities held by North Vietnam
To clear land for new farms after the war
To stop refugees leaving the country by boat
a.why: The herbicides stripped leaves from forests so that enemy troops had less cover. They were not used to clear farmland for peacetime use, and they had nothing to do with stopping refugees, who mostly left after 1975.
a.clue: Think about what thick forest gave to soldiers.

b.q: Linh's family fled Vietnam by boat in 1979 and later settled in Melbourne. What does this show about the effects of the conflict?
opts: It caused many people to leave and resettle abroad
It ended all movement of people out of Vietnam
It was limited to people who had fought in the war
It left Australia with no link to Indochina
b.why: Many people left Indochina after the war, and some were resettled in Australia. The conflict did not end movement out of Vietnam, and its effects reached well beyond the soldiers who fought.
b.clue: Look at where the family ended up.

a.best: To remove forest cover that hid enemy troops

b.best: It caused many people to leave and resettle abroad

problems.detail: The three wrong options are implausible for Year 12 HSC students. 'No link to Indochina' is contradicted by the stem itself, and 'ended all movement' and 'limited to people who had fought' are easily dismissed, so the question tests little.

check.summary: The facts on the card, the answers and the explanations are accurate. Question b is too easy for Year 12 because its wrong options are obviously false, one of them contradicted by the question stem.

To stop refugees leaving the country by boat

b.q: Linh's family fled Vietnam by boat in 1979 and later settled in Melbourne. Which conclusion does their story best support?
opts: People kept leaving after 1975, and some came to Australia
Most refugees left Vietnam before Saigon fell in 1975
Its effects ended when the fighting in Vietnam stopped
Refugees came only from Vietnam, not Laos or Cambodia
b.why: Linh's family left in 1979, years after the fighting in Vietnam ended in 1975, and settled in Australia. This fits the wider pattern of people leaving after 1975. One family from Vietnam cannot show that refugees came only from Vietnam, and many also left Laos and Cambodia.
b.clue: Compare the year the family left with 1975.
